correctness.rationale: Compact Kraus operators induce compact maps B(H) to B(H) by norm approximation with finite-rank Kraus operators. In their common finite-dimensional support, the paired maps are Hilbert–Schmidt adjoints, so their nonzero spectra have conjugate algebraic multiplicities; Riesz projection perturbation preserves this in the compact norm limit. The standard positive-map norm identity yields the joint radius formulas. The Krein–Rutman positive compact operator theorem yields positive eigenoperators for positive radii. Grouping all compact length-m words proves the power statement. The Fock witness is computed exactly. The packaged checker passed 1,584 finite diagnostic assertions; infinite-dimensional facts rely on the proof.

originality.rationale: The direct prior result is finite-matrix row/column radius equality (Scherer–Shalit–Shamovich, 2026, Example 5.2), with an unrestricted infinite-dimensional counterexample. The new claim strengthens this on infinite-dimensional compact-Kraus tuples to conjugate nonzero spectra with multiplicities, positive compact eigenoperators, and extends to tuples with compact words. Primary full texts and relevant published records did not identify an implication covering those claims, subject to residual broader elementary-map spectral priority risk.
residual_risks: General compact elementary-operator or completely positive-map spectral-duality results may imply the statement without row/column wording; publication priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The result identifies an infinite-dimensional class on which the sharp known row/column discrepancy disappears, exhibits the compact-word threshold even with noncompact entries, and upgrades a numerical coincidence to spectral multiset reciprocity and positive compact eigenoperators. The finite-section approximation is useful despite failure of general spectral-radius continuity; it is structurally linked to the recent operator-space theory rather than a bespoke finite computation.
